Rashi on Gittin 60a:10:1.hebrew: אף היא - הילני המלכה, במסכת יומא (ד' לז.):
Rashi on Gittin 60a:10:1.english: She also - [This refers to] Queen Helene, in Tractate Yoma (37a):

Rashi on Gittin 60a:10:2.english: The portion of a sotah - To write from there portions for sotot who come [in the future]:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:10:3.english: In alef-beit - That is to say, [only] the first letters of the words:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:11:1.english: When he writes - [This refers to] the priest who writes the sotah passage:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:11:2.english: Like that which is written - According to the signs, he would understand [the text] and write [it]:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:12:1.hebrew: אם שכב - כלומר, "ואת כי שטית וגו'":
Rashi on Gittin 60a:12:1.english: If [a man] lay [with you] - that is to say, [the verse], "And you, if you have gone aside, etc." [Numbers 5:20]:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:12:2.hebrew: בסירוגין - תחילת המקרא היה כתוב תיבה שלימה, ולבסוף ראשי תיבות:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:12:2.english: Alternatingly - [At] the beginning of the verse it was written [as] a complete word, and at the end [as] initials:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:13:1.english: Until "And it came to pass on the eighth day" - for it is the end of the commandment of the offerings:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:14:1.hebrew: אז אמרתי - כך אמר דוד: "אז אמרתי" — כשערערו עלי שאול ודואג לפוסלני מלבא בקהל, והועד בבית המדרש "עמוני ולא עמונית", כדאמרינן ביבמות (דף עז.):
Rashi on Gittin 60a:14:1.english: Then I said - Thus said David: "Then I said" — when Saul and Doeg challenged me to disqualify me from entering the congregation, and it was testified in the study hall, "An Ammonite [male], and not an Ammonitess," as we state in Yevamot (77a):

Rashi on Gittin 60a:14:2.english: Behold, I have come - Now I have entered the fold [of the congregation]:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:14:3.hebrew: כתוב עלי - מאז ניתנה התורה הוזכרתי בה: "ואת שתי בנותיך הנמצאות" (בראשית י״ט:ט״ו) — בזכות דוד שעתיד לצאת מרות המואביה, ונעמה העמונית אמו של רחבעם. כתיב הכא "הנמצאות", וכתיב התם (תהלים פט) "מצאתי דוד עבדי". אלמא מגילה איקרי, משום דמתחילה נכתבה מגילת בראשית, והדר מגילת נח, והדר מגילת אברהם; והיינו דקאמר: במגילת אברהם "כתוב עלי":
Rashi on Gittin 60a:14:3.english: Written of me - From [the time] the Torah was given, I was mentioned in it: "and your two daughters who are found [here]" (Genesis 19:15) — in the merit of David, who was destined to descend from Ruth the Moabite, and [in the merit of] Naamah the Ammonite, mother of Rehoboam. It is written here "who are found," and it is written there (Psalms 89[:21]): "I have found David My servant." Thus [we see that a section of the Torah] is called a "scroll," because at first the Scroll of Genesis was written, and then the Scroll of Noah, and then the Scroll of Abraham; and this is what [David] meant: in the Scroll of Abraham "it is written of me":

Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:1.hebrew: א"נ לכדרבי לוי - איקראי התורה מגילה: אותן ח' פרשיות שהוצרכו ליום, נאמרו ונכתבו ונמסרו בו ביום, ונכתבו כל אחת במגילה לבדה, לפי שמובדלות ורחוקות זו מזו. הלכך קרי לשאר נמי מגילה, משום דכשחזר משה והשלימה, הוצרך לכתוב מבראשית עד פרשת כהנים לבד, ודילג פרשת כהנים הכתובה כבר, וכתב מפרשת כהנים עד פרשת שילוח טמאים, וכן כולם:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:1.english: Alternatively, [this alludes] to [the statement] of Rabbi Levi - [the Torah] is called a scroll [for the following reason]: Those eight sections that were needed for [that] day were said, written, and transmitted on that very day, and each one was written on a scroll by itself, because they are separated and distant from one another. Therefore, [Scripture] also calls the rest [of the Torah] a scroll, because when [Moses] later returned and completed it, he had to write from Bereishit [Genesis] until the section of the priests separately, and he skipped the section of the priests that was already written, and wrote from the section of the priests until the section of the sending away of the impure, and so too [with] all of them:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:2.hebrew: פרשת כהנים - "אמור אל הכהנים", שהלכות כהנים כתובות בה: לא יטמא, לא יקח, מום בו לא יגש. ומפני שבו ביום הוזקק לעבודה, הוצרכה קדושתן להודיעם:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:2.english: The section of the priests - [This is the section beginning] "Speak to the priests" (Leviticus 21:1), in which the laws of the priests are written: [that] he shall not become ritually impure, he shall not take [a disqualified woman in marriage], [and one who has] a blemish in him shall not approach [to offer sacrifices]. And because on that very day [the priest] was required for the [Tabernacle] service, it was necessary to inform them of their sanctity:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:3.hebrew: פרשת לוים - "קח (נא) את הלוים" דבהעלותך, שבה הל כות לוים. וי"א: "ואל הלוים תדבר", ואינו כן, כי מה עניינם אצל הקמת המשכן? מעשר ראשון לא נהגה עד סוף חמשים וארבעה שנה; ועוד, "פרשת מעשר" מיקריא:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:3.english: The section of the Levites - [This refers to the passage,] "Take (please) the Levites" [Numbers 8:6] in [the Torah portion of] Beha'alotcha, for in it are the laws of the Levites. And some say [it refers to], "And to the Levites you shall speak" [Numbers 18:26]. But this is not so, for what do they have to do with the erection of the Tabernacle? [The law of] the first tithe did not take effect until the end of fifty-four years; and furthermore, [that passage] is called "the section of the tithe":

Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:4.hebrew: פרשת לוים - הוצרכה לבו ביום, שנזקקו לשיר:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:4.english: The section of the Levites - It was needed for that very day, because they were required for the song:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:5.hebrew: פרשת טמאים - "ויהי אנשים וגו'", משום הלכות הפסח; והמשכן הוקם באחד בניסן, והוזהרה להם פרשת שילוח טמאים — "וישלחו מן המחנה" — שבו ביום הוקבעו שלש מחנות: מחנה שכינה, ומחנה לויה, ומחנה ישראל, והוזקקו להשתלח. ומתוך כך הוזקקו טמאים לישאל: הואיל וצריכין שילוח ולא יוכלו ליכנס למשכן, היאך יעשו פסחיהם? ולרבי לוי, יכולים היו ליטהר עד ט"ו, ולא נזקקו לפסח שני אלא א"כ לא יטהרו:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:5.english: The section of the impure - [This refers to the passage] "And there were certain men, etc." [Numbers 9:6], [which was said] because of the laws of the Passover offering. For the Tabernacle was erected on the first of Nisan, and [on that day] they were commanded the section of the sending away of the impure — "that they send out of the camp" [Numbers 5:2] — since on that very day the three camps were established: the camp of the Divine Presence, the camp of the Levites, and the camp of Israel, and [the impure] were required to be sent out. Consequently, the impure [individuals] needed to inquire: Since they require sending away and cannot enter the Tabernacle, how shall they offer their Passover sacrifices? And according to Rabbi Levi, they were able to become pure by the fifteenth [of Nisan], and would not have needed the second Passover unless they did not become pure:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:6.hebrew: ופרשת שילוח טמאים - "וישלחו מן המחנה", שבאותו היום הוקבעו המחנות; וכשנגללים הפרוכת בכל סילוק מסעות, הותרו זבין ומצורעים ליכנס לשם:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:6.english: And the section of the sending away of the impure - [This refers to the passage,] "That they send out of the camp" [Numbers 5:2], for on that day the camps were established; and when the curtains [of the Tabernacle] are rolled up at every dismantling for journeys, zavim [men with a genital discharge] and metzoraim [lepers] were permitted to enter there:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:7.hebrew: ופרשת אחרי מות - אע"פ שהיא של יום הכפורים, בו ביום נאמרה, כדכתיב "אחרי מות", ומפני שמתו בני אהרן בשביל ביאה שלא לצורך, נאמרה אותה אזהרה לאהרן: "אל יבא בכל עת":
Rashi on Gittin 60a:17:7.english: And the section [beginning] "After the death" - Even though it pertains to Yom Kippur, it was said on that very day, as it is written: "After the death [of the two sons of Aaron]"; and because Aaron's sons died due to an unwarranted entry, that warning was stated to Aaron: "let him not enter at all times":

Rashi on Gittin 60a:1:1.hebrew: מי קוראין - כלומר, תיקנו שום סדר לישראל בשבתות משום דרכי שלום:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:1:1.english: Who reads - That is to say, [did] they institute any order for Israelites on Shabbatot on account of the ways of peace?

Rashi on Gittin 60a:1:2.hebrew: הראויין לימנות כו' - דאמרינן במסכת שבת [באלו קשרים] (דף קיד.): איזהו תלמיד חכם שראוי למנותו פרנס על הצבור? כל ששואלין אותו דבר הלכה בכל מקום ואומרה:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:1:2.english: Who are fit to be appointed, etc. - For we say in Tractate Shabbat, in [the chapter] Eilu Kesharim (114a): "Who is a Torah scholar who is fit to be appointed as a leader of the community? Anyone whom they ask a matter of halakhah in any place, and he states it:"

Rashi on Gittin 60a:2:1.hebrew: בחומשין - שיש שכותבין להן חמשה חומשין, כל חומש אחד שלם לעצמו, וכל ספריהם היו במגילה כס"ת שלנו:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:2:1.english: From chumashim - for there are [those] who write for themselves the five books [of the Torah], each book [as] one complete [scroll] by itself, and all of their books were in a scroll like our Torah scroll:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:3:1.hebrew: מחסר במילתיה - שקורין לו ס"ת, וחסר הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:3:1.english: It is lacking in its matter - for they call it a Torah scroll, and it is incomplete:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:4:1.english: Because it was not permitted to be written - [anything] less than one complete book by itself:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:6:1.hebrew: והא לא ניתן ליכתב - שום דבר גמרא והלכה ואגדה, כדאמרינן לקמן: "אלה אתה כותב" כו':
Rashi on Gittin 60a:6:1.english: And it was not permitted to be written - any matter of Gemara, halachah, or aggadah, as we say later: "These you may write," etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:6:2.hebrew: כיון דלא אפשר - מליכתב, שנתמעט הלב והתורה משתכחת:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:6:2.english: Since it is not possible - [to refrain] from writing [it], for the heart [i.e., memory] has diminished and the Torah is being forgotten:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:6:3.hebrew: עת לעשות לה' - ואם בא עת לעשות תקנה לשם שמים, הפרו דברי תורה לשעה הצריכה:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:6:3.english: It is time to act for the Lord - And if a time comes to make an enactment for the sake of Heaven, [one may] nullify words of Torah for the needed hour:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:6:4.hebrew: ה"נ כיון דלא אפשר - שאין לכל צבור וצבור יכולת לכתוב נביאים שלם:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:6:4.english: Here too, since it is not possible - for not every congregation has the ability to write a complete [scroll of the] Prophets:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:7:1.english: A scroll - A single portion of the Torah, or two:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:8:1.english: According to the one who says - [this is stated] later in our sugya:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:8:2.hebrew: מגילה מגילה ניתנה - כשנאמרה פרשה למשה, היה כותבה, ולבסוף מ' שנה, כשנגמרו כל הפרשיות, חיברן בגידין ותפרן:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:8:2.english: [The Torah] was given scroll by scroll - When a passage was spoken to Moses, he would write it [down], and at the end of forty years, when all the passages were completed, he joined them with sinews and sewed them [together]:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:9:1.hebrew: חתומה ניתנה - לא נכתבה עד סוף מ' שנה, לאחר שנאמרו כל הפרשיות כולן; והנאמרות לו בשנה ראשונה ושניה היו סדורות לו על פה עד שכתבן:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:9:1.english: [The Torah] was given complete - It was not written until the end of the forty [years], after all the sections had been stated [to Moses]; and those [sections] stated to him in the first and second year[s] were arranged for him orally until he wrote them:

Rashi on Gittin 60a:9:2.hebrew: לפי שאין כותבין - ואפי' למ"ד מגילה מגילה ניתנה, כיון דאידבק אידבק:
Rashi on Gittin 60a:9:2.english: Because one may not write [separate scrolls] - And even according to the one who says [that the Torah] was given scroll by scroll, once it was joined together, it remained joined together.

Tosafot on Gittin 60a:12:1.hebrew: אם שכב אם לא שכב - "אם שכב" לא כתיב כלל, אלא "אם לא שכב" כתיב, אלא דבתר הכי כתיב "ואת כי שטית":
Tosafot on Gittin 60a:12:1.english: If [a man] lay, if he did not lay - "If [a man] lay" is not written [in the Torah] at all; rather, "if he did not lay" is written, except that afterward it is written, "but if you have gone astray":

Tosafot on Gittin 60a:14:1.hebrew: תורה חתומה ניתנה - תימה, דכתיב (שמות כ״ד:ז׳): "ויקח ספר הברית ויקרא באזני העם", ופרש"י בפי' חומש דהיינו מבראשית ועד כאן. ונראה לפרש, דלא קאמר "חתומה ניתנה" שלא נכתבה עד לבסוף, אלא שעל הסדר נכתבה; דיש פרשיות שנאמרו תחילה לפני אותם הכתובים לפניהם, ולא נכתבה עד שנאמר לו אותה שכתובה לפניה, וכותב זאת אחריה. ועל זה מייתי מדרבי לוי, שאותם לא נאמרו על הסדר; והיה יכול להוכיח זה מכמה מקראות, דאין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה, אלא הואיל ומשכח דרבי לוי, מייתי לה. ור"ת גריס: א"ר לוי, מילתא באפי נפשה:
Tosafot on Gittin 60a:14:1.english: The Torah was given as a complete [book] - [This is] astonishing, for it is written (Exodus 24:7): "And he took the book of the covenant and read [it] in the ears of the people," and Rashi explained in [his] commentary on the Chumash that this means from Genesis until here. And it seems [proper] to explain that he does not mean [by] "it was given as a complete [book]" that it was not written until the end, but rather that it was written in order; for there are sections that were said earlier, before those that are written before them, and [such a section] was not written until the one written before it was said to him, and then he would write this one after it. And regarding this [the Gemara] cites [the statement] of Rabbi Levi, [to show] that those [sections] were not said in order. And it could have proved this from several verses, [showing] that there is no chronological order in the Torah, except that since it found [the statement] of Rabbi Levi, it cites it. And Rabbeinu Tam reads [the text as]: "Rabbi Levi said," [as] an independent statement:

Tosafot on Gittin 60a:17:1.hebrew: פרשת טמאים - פי' בקונטרס: "ויהי אנשים". וקשה לפירושו, דאמר בפ"ק דפסחים (דף ו.): שואלים בהלכות פסח קודם הפסח ל' יום, שהרי נביא עומד בפסח ראשון ומזהיר על פסח שני; ולפ"ז איכא חדש וחצי, כיון שנאמר בראש חדש ניסן. ועוד, דלא יתכן לרבי יוסי הגלילי דאמר: נושאי ארונו של יוסף היו, ולרבי יצחק דאמר: למת מצוה נטמאו, וחל שביעי שלהם בערב פסח. ונראה דפרשת טמאים היינו פרשת "וינזרו" (ויקרא כב), דכתיב ביה טומאת שרץ ונבילה וכל הצריך לטומאת מקדש וקדשיו:
Tosafot on Gittin 60a:17:1.english: The section of the impure - Rashi explained [that this refers to the passage] "And there were men [who were impure]." And this is difficult according to his explanation, for [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Pesaḥim (6a): One inquires about the laws of Passover thirty days before Passover, as the prophet stands on the first Passover and warns about the second Passover; and according to this, there is a month and a half, since it was said on Rosh Ḥodesh Nisan. Furthermore, [this] is not possible according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who says: They were the bearers of Joseph's coffin, and according to Rabbi Yitzḥak, who says: They became impure through a met mitzvah [an unattended corpse], and their seventh [day of purification] fell on the eve of Passover. Rather, it appears that "the section of the impure" is the section [beginning] "Let them separate" (Leviticus 22), in which is written the impurity of a creeping creature and an animal carcass, and everything necessary for the impurity of the Temple and its consecrated [food]:

Tosafot on Gittin 60a:17:2.hebrew: ופרשת אחרי מות - בבראשית רבה איכא פלוגתא גבי "אחר הדברים האלה היה דבר ה' אל אברם" (בראשית ט״ו:א׳), דאיכא למ"ד "אחר" סמוך ו"אחרי" מופלג, ואיכא למ"ד איפכא. וקשה מ"אחרי מות", דבו ביום היה. ושמא נאמר אחר כל הפרשיות, לכך חשיב מופלג:
Tosafot on Gittin 60a:17:2.english: And the section “After the death” - In Bereishit Rabbah there is a dispute regarding [the verse,] “After [aḥar] these things the word of the Lord came to Abram” (Genesis 15:1), for there is one who says “aḥar” [indicates] immediate [proximity] and “aḥarei” [indicates] distant, and there is one who says the opposite. And it is difficult from “After [aḥarei] the death,” for it was on that very day. And perhaps it was said after all the [other] sections, therefore it is considered distant:
